title: NNC2215 macrocycle proxy coordinate package
purpose: Public record of the Dia Health One generated macrocycle and glucose proxy coordinates. These are model-generated geometry inputs for a clearly labelled proxy study. They are not the 2026 in-house crystal structure, not full NNC2215 and not simulation outputs.

status_terms.basis: public 2024 author-built models (Figshare 26526460) and the Nature Extended Data Fig. 8i macrocycle graph

artifacts.label: Macrocycle proxy, tricarboxylate microstate
artifacts.role: Constrained macrocycle built on the open-model heavy-atom coordinates
artifacts.microstate_assumption: Three aryl carboxylates deprotonated at pH 7.4; ureas and azide neutral. Matches the deprotonated carboxylates recorded in both model PDBs.
artifacts.generation: RDKit ETKDGv3 embedding (randomSeed 2215) with the open-model mapped heavy atoms used as an explicit coordinate map (CoordMap), Kabsch-aligned to the model frame, then MMFF94 minimisation with 100 kcal/mol/A^2 position restraints on the mapped atoms.
artifacts.rmsd_to_open_model_A: restrained to the mapped open-model heavy atoms (reported as reproduced positionally; not an independent structural refinement)
artifacts.note: Roof methyl carbons take the model C27/C29 positions; the propyl-azide tail carbons C22-C23 and N3 are newly embedded. This is a model-generated geometry, not an author coordinate set.

artifacts.label: Glucose reference pose
artifacts.role: Beta-D-glucose reference pose taken from the open model
artifacts.stereo_check: 3D-assigned stereochemistry canonicalises to the same SMILES as beta-D-glucopyranose.
artifacts.note: The glucose reference pose and the constrained macrocycle overlap at this geometry (minimum heavy-atom separation 0.504 A, centroid separation 0.958 A). This is reported as measured: it is the same steric overlap that causes every rigid PaG conformer to be rejected below, and it means the two published model components cannot be used together as a bound glucose complex without a documented pose protocol.
artifacts.source: Open-model residue BGLC (chain D, 24 atoms including hydrogens)

excess_carbon_audit.finding: Both public model PDBs carry a 64-carbon macrocycle heavy-element pool against the Fig 8i C56 macrocycle graph (the roof ring has 2-carbon ethyl substituents where the figure draws methyls).
excess_carbon_audit.resolution_in_proxy: The proxy macrocycle is built from the Fig 8i C56 neutral graph; the two excess roof-ethyl terminal carbons are removed for graph isomorphism. Their positions remain a documented model inference, not an author atom map.

pag_pose.reason: The pre-registered glucose-mimetic placement hypothesis did not hold for this macrocycle geometry. 300 ETKDGv3 PaG conformers were generated and rigidly aligned to the 11 mapped glucose ring atoms; every conformer had a heavy-atom clash with the macrocycle. Minimum heavy-atom distances were 0.27, 0.45, 1.04, 1.11 and 1.23 A at the min, 10th, 50th, 90th and 100th percentiles.
pag_pose.pre_registered_filter: Reject any conformer with a PaG heavy atom closer than 2.0 A to a macrocycle heavy atom; fallback threshold 1.6 A. Zero conformers passed either filter.
pag_pose.consequence: The failure is a result about the pose hypothesis, so no PaG coordinate is published. PaG placement remains an open gate and needs either author coordinates or a separately pre-registered strategy.

what_this_does_not_establish: That these coordinates reproduce the 2026 in-house crystal structure.
That the macrocycle bond orders, stereochemistry, protonation or charges are validated.
Any glucose or PaG binding affinity, selectivity or receptor activity.
A simulation-ready topology or force field.

provenance.environment_note: Local research environment; the interactive viewer reads the published coordinates directly and does not prepare or validate chemistry.
